A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching title, authors, algorithm, and principal theorems. Their main text, equations, explanatory figure, and complete Appendices A-C are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical convergence guarantees, and mathematical proofs, including in Appendices A-C. Figure 1 is a conceptual illustration; no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v3 remains a theoretical paper throughout the main text and Appendices A-C. Its added nonsmooth convergence remark is mathematical, and no original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the extrapolated-gradient hint, and the constant and adaptive step-size procedures are unchanged. The standard optimistic-gradient update added in Section 3.2 explicitly illustrates an alternative already discussed in v1; it does not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or reports experimental task evaluations. The added nonsmooth setting is a theoretical extension, not newly evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical comparison methods. The additional cited optimization methods expand related work rather than introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, or training budgets. The retained parameter prescriptions concern theoretical convergence analysis.

E4.justification: Ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity studies, and empirical case analyses are absent from both versions, including their appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Expectations and variance bounds are theoretical assumptions and guarantees, not empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries, measured performance values, or experimental findings are added or revised. The new nonsmooth complexity statement is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 adds Remark 3.1, stating O(epsilon^-3 delta^-1) complexity for finding (delta, epsilon)-stationary points under bounded gradient second moments. It sketches an adaptation using Theorem 8 of CMO23 and the existing regret bound. The smooth-case theorems and substantive proofs in Appendices A-C are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: a doubly optimistic method eliminating the fixed-point subroutine and attaining O(epsilon^-1.75 + sigma^2 epsilon^-3.5), together with an adaptive step-size variant. The nonsmooth remark remains a supplementary claim.

C2.justification: Remark 3.1 newly presents Algorithm 1 as applicable to nonsmooth optimization, qualifying this extension with bounded second moments and a different stationarity criterion. The discussion of remaining parameter dependence and future fully adaptive methods is unchanged.

D1.justification: The algorithmic details and parameter prescriptions in Sections 3-4 and Appendices B-C are retained. No implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data access information is added; the nonsmooth remark does not specify concrete new parameter choices.

R1.justification: Sections 1-1.1 add All18a, All18b, TSJRJ18, FLZ19, and ZLJSJ20 to the discussion of stochastic and nonsmooth optimization. Appendix C.1 newly attributes the existing Lemma C.1 to KLBC19, AKC22, and LYC18. The central positioning relative to CMO23 and JMP25 is retained.

P1.justification: v3 expands author-name citations, adds equal-contribution credit and an acknowledgment, corrects the explanatory iteration indices in Section 3.1, and adds limited explanatory text in Section 3.2 and Remark 3.1. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Several previously inline bounds, including those in Lemmas 3.1, 3.2, and 4.1, become separate equation displays. Figure 1 is slightly enlarged, and floats and surrounding text reflow. The figure's content and Algorithm 1 are retained, with no new plots or tables.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and attribution through the explicit standard optimistic update in Section 3.2, more readable equation displays, broader related-work coverage, and source attribution for Lemma C.1. The central algorithm and smooth-case analysis are retained. The nonsmooth extension is presented only through a short proof sketch, so the added theoretical support is limited.
